results.update: The carrier's appraiser issued the signed award on Sept 26 after the revised position was accepted and the appraisal invoice was paid; the file is settled and now waiting on the insurance payment to be issued.

timeline.event: Joseph's office asked the newly named carrier's appraiser for his umpire list and a preferred date for a solo inspection.
The carrier's appraiser Reggie Morgan confirmed his assignment on the claim and sent his umpire candidate list.
Reggie Morgan proposed a solo inspection for August 5; it was added to the calendar pending the homeowner's confirmation.
The homeowner confirmed the August 5 inspection time.
Reggie Morgan confirmed the inspection and asked for Joseph's umpire selection.
Joseph sent his list of proposed umpires.
Ty Patch was agreed on as umpire and the Declaration of Appraisers was signed.
Joseph sent his position: the estimate, ESX file, and photo report.
The carrier's appraiser's solo inspection of the property took place as scheduled.
The carrier's appraiser sent his position estimate.

Joseph reviewed the estimate and asked for several items to be added: supervision hours, an extra felt layer, splash guards, window screens, drip edge, chimney chase and flue cap repairs, and starter shingles.
The carrier's appraiser sent a revised estimate addressing most items, noting only six damaged screens instead of eight, and asked if the new position was acceptable.
Joseph sent the appraisal invoice to the contractor.
The contractor confirmed the appraisal invoice had been paid.
Joseph told the carrier's appraiser the revised estimate looked good and asked him to send the award.
Joseph confirmed again that everything on the file looked good.
The carrier's appraiser sent the signed award.

results.update: Joseph agreed to the umpire's numbers on Sept 25 and asked for the award; the umpire is now gathering final comments from the carrier's appraiser before issuing it. The insured has already paid the appraisal invoice in full.

timeline.event: The carrier's appraiser (Crawford & Company) introduced himself as newly assigned to the claim and proposed umpire candidates.
Wade Wells was agreed on as umpire, and a joint inspection was scheduled for March 10.
The joint inspection was held with the carrier's appraiser on site.
The carrier's appraiser sent his position estimate for review.

Joseph reviewed the carrier's position and requested revisions to several exterior, garage, and interior items; the carrier's appraiser said the two positions were over $100,000 apart and raised invoking the umpire.
Joseph agreed to invoke the umpire.
Joseph and the carrier's adjuster reached an impasse and requested the umpire's assistance; the umpire acknowledged and asked the carrier's adjuster for his position and file information.

The carrier's adjuster sent his position and photo report, noting general agreement on the exterior and garage scope but a significant disagreement over the interior dwelling scope, and said some of Joseph's noted concerns appeared related to prior structural movement rather than the loss.
The umpire asked whether a joint or solo inspection was preferred; Joseph said a joint inspection was needed to present arguments about porous materials and soot in the wall cavities.
The carrier's adjuster agreed to a joint inspection and asked the umpire to propose dates.
The umpire sent invoices for the umpire fee to both parties and said he would schedule the inspection once payment was received from both sides; Joseph offered August 3 at 9:30 AM.
The carrier's adjuster confirmed receipt of the invoice and agreed to August 3 at 9:30 AM pending the umpire's confirmation.
The umpire fee invoice was sent to the homeowner; the umpire confirmed August 3 at 9:30 AM on his calendar, and the homeowner confirmed availability with interior access.
The carrier's adjuster confirmed he would attend the August 3 inspection.
The umpire said he had not yet received payment from either the carrier or the homeowner and suggested postponing the inspection.

Joseph asked not to reschedule due to other commitments and said he would stress to the homeowner the importance of paying promptly; the umpire confirmed the homeowner's payment was received but said he could not attend the inspection the next day without the carrier's payment, so it would need to be rescheduled.
The umpire asked for availability on August 10 or 12; Joseph and the carrier's adjuster agreed on August 12 at 2:00 PM.
The August 12 inspection at 2:00 PM was confirmed on all calendars, and the homeowner confirmed availability.
The umpire said the carrier's payment still had not been received and asked the carrier's adjuster to follow up.
Joseph sent his file information to the carrier's adjuster following the joint inspection, who confirmed receipt.
The umpire noted the carrier's payment still had not been received; the carrier's adjuster said he would follow up.
The carrier's adjuster said he had spoken with the carrier again about the outstanding umpire payment and apologized for the continued delay.
The carrier's adjuster reported the carrier issued payment to the umpire, who said he would confirm once it arrives.
The umpire confirmed he received payment and said he would provide his position for review in the coming business days.
The umpire circulated his position on the file and asked both parties to review and respond, offering to schedule a call if needed.
Joseph agreed the umpire's proposed numbers were fair and reasonable and asked for the award to be sent, noting a few items he would still like added.
Joseph sent the appraisal invoice to the homeowner requesting payment via Zelle, Stripe, Venmo, or check; the homeowner confirmed payment was sent via Zelle.
Joseph's office confirmed receipt of the invoice payment; the homeowner asked how and when to expect the insurance settlement check.
The umpire asked the carrier's appraiser for his comments before finalizing the award.

results.update: The carrier's appraiser sent his award and estimate on Sept 3; the file is otherwise complete, but the appraisal invoice sent to the contractor on Sept 12 remains unpaid after two follow-ups.
results.needed: Pay the outstanding appraisal invoice, sent Sept 12 and followed up on twice since, which remains unpaid.

timeline.event: The appraisal demand letter was sent to the homeowner to begin the appraisal process.
The formal appraisal demand and estimate were sent to the carrier; Homeowners of America Insurance Company agreed to proceed with the appraisal process and named its appraiser.
Joseph's office asked the carrier's appraiser for his umpire list and a preferred date for a solo inspection.
The carrier's appraiser proposed September 2 at 11:00 AM for the solo inspection; the homeowner confirmed.
The carrier's appraiser asked to move the inspection to 12:00 PM; the homeowner confirmed the new time.
The carrier's appraiser's solo inspection took place as scheduled.
Joseph sent his file information to the carrier's appraiser.
The carrier's appraiser sent his award and estimate for the claim.
The carrier's appraiser followed up on the appraisal award and estimate submitted for this claim.
Joseph sent the appraisal invoice to the contractor for processing.
Joseph's office followed up with the contractor for an update on the invoice payment status.
Joseph's office followed up again with the contractor, noting the appraisal invoice remained unpaid and asking when payment could be expected.

results.update: The carrier already issued the final depreciation payment on 6/30, which the contractor confirmed with a photo of the check on Sept 21; Joseph's public-adjusting invoice sent Sept 20 remains unpaid despite a Sept 25 follow-up.
results.needed: Pay the outstanding public-adjusting fee invoice sent Sept 20, which remains unpaid.

timeline.event: The contractor (Legacy Roofing) sent Joseph the roof damage report and the homeowner's contact information.
Joseph's office moved the file to a public-adjuster agreement since the carrier had been difficult and was refusing to proceed with appraisal.
The file was pending assignment, with the carrier's adjuster expected to reach out the following week for a reinspection.
A reinspection with the carrier's adjuster was scheduled for the following Monday.
The carrier's field adjuster asked to speak by phone to agree on a scope of work.
The estimate and photos were sent to the insurance company; the file was awaiting their assessment.
The carrier (Homesite/AFICS) issued the final recoverable-depreciation payment.

Joseph requested release of the recoverable depreciation, noting the repairs were complete; after five weeks with no response, the carrier confirmed on Sept 2 that payment had already been sent on 6/30 and the check had been cashed.
Joseph asked the contractor whether the homeowner had received or deposited the depreciation check, since it never came through the office.
Joseph sent the public-adjusting invoice for this file to the contractor and the homeowner.
The contractor sent a photo of the depreciation check for the file.
Joseph's office followed up with the contractor and homeowner on the payment status of the unpaid invoice.
